name: notion-review-to-company-logo

deploy.description: Notion Customer Review webhook -> set the review page's icon to the reviewer company's logo from logo.dev, resolved via the review's Company rollup (Contact -> Related Company) and the company's Website. Migration of the classic 'Add Logo to Customer Review'. Empty pings skip; an unrecognised page shape throws.

trigger.trigger_note: Catch hook, matching the classic Zap's trigger. The sender is a Notion automation on the Customer Reviews data source. `webhook_url` is filled in by the publish pipeline on first publish and is the URL that automation must be repointed at; `trigger_url` is Zapier-internal and cannot be called by Notion.

notion.note: Pages are read with sdk.fetch and the icon is written with a PATCH to /v1/pages/{id}, matching the rest of this repo. The Notion actions cannot write an icon at all: `update_page` takes only page + content, and the classic Zap reached for a per-account Custom Action instead.

logo_dev.note: Publishable key (pk_), carried over from the classic Zap. Designed for client-side image URLs and already public — it is embedded in every review page icon this Zap has ever set. Not a secret.

icon_policy.note: Every run sets the icon, replacing hand-picked custom emoji or uploaded-file icons on a re-trigger. The only skipped write is a byte-identical one. The alternative considered and rejected was fill-only (set when absent, refresh only our own logo.dev URL).

cutover.classic_zap_state: paused in full as of the 2026-09-06 export (every node paused: true), so there is no double-write window and this ships enabled
cutover.status: pending — the Customer Reviews automation in Notion must be repointed at this Zap's webhook_url before anything reaches it

classic_zap_note: The classic Zap had been unable to resolve a company for some time: its step 3 searched Companies for a `Clay Contacts` relation containing the trigger's contact, and Companies carries no such property any more (the live relation is `Contacts`). Exactly one of 11 review pages carries a logo.dev icon, which is the only run it is known to have completed. Its final step was the per-account Custom Action ae:373967 'Add Page Icon to Notion Page'; the durable replaces it with a direct PATCH so nothing outside this repo has to stay configured.
